notes: MP relied on alleged verbal advice from PDS (not IPSA); PDS held no record (para 15). Officer says nothing new versus IPSA appeal (paras 25, 33) yet cites PDS records (paras 28, 30). Bright-line: IPSA budgets exclude IT (para 29).

guidance_change_note: No recommendation made; officer notes the 18th edition independently lifted the newsletter ban shortly after the claim (paras 21, 39i).
notes: IPSA held correct (paras 33-35) yet altered to 50/50 cost split on mitigation (paras 44-46); para 48 disclaims precedent. Para 34 vs 44 conflict on new information. Judging party-political wording needed judgment, so not bright-line.

general_reading: A cost failing any one fundamental principle is not claimable; a staff festive meal out has no parliamentary purpose, even when held after a parliamentary away day (paras 25, 37).
guidance_change_note: IPSA conceded the festive guidance caused confusion and said it would update it to state team meals out are not claimable hospitality (para 19).
notes: Tip (£40.19) separately barred by explicit no-tips rule (para 28). Main claim turned on unclear festive guidance and parliamentary-purpose judgment, so not bright-line. Away-day evidence post-dated initial rejection (paras 21, 36), though para 24 calls it nothing fundamentally new.

Retrospective contingency bid for storage past approved end date (paras 5-7). MP believed costs pre-authorised (paras 9, 22); Officer found time limit clearly communicated, no new information (paras 28-33, 36). Exceptional-circumstances test is discretionary, so not bright-line.

general_reading: 'Exceptional' (undefined in Scheme) read in dictionary sense of unusual/not typical; choosing rent that absorbs the whole budget, or rising energy bills, is not exceptional (para 24a).
notes: Panel refusal held correct on all three para 10.8 factors, yet officer let MP claim up to unused 2022-23 budget (346.85) after consulting IPSA CEO (paras 24-27). Officer analysed bills obtained at review (para 21). Discretionary multi-factor test.

CO finds IPSA's repayment demand correct on information then held (para 31) but directs no repayment via para 10.19 discretion; CEO and CO state no precedent (paras 38-39). Original decision applied numeric budget cap. Text cites 10.16 at para 36.

Contingency refusal for utilities overspend; exceptionality is a judgment test, so not bright-line. Officer's own energy-price research used (para 28). Paras 26, 30 restate onus and no carry-forward of service overspends. Para 9 says 2020/21; title says 2021/22.

Rejection held correct under receipt deadlines (paras 29, 34) but credit note rescinded on discretion (paras 36-39); receipts came after rejection (para 16). Bright-line: deadline rule. Recommendation is MP-specific training only. Repeat-transaction argument (para 13) not treated as past practice.

Eleventh edition applied (paras 3, 7); footnote cites Twelfth. Panel waived 721.52 of 1289.17; Officer confirmed remaining 567.65 repayable, seeing double rent as personal choice (para 22). Account manager's support attached (para 14), not expressly weighed. Contingency test discretionary.

Summary only: resolved informally before full review; IPSA itself reversed after officer obtained card statement and phone bill (para 4), so no formal officer determination. Original rejection followed mechanically from missing receipt. Amount not stated.

guidance_change_note: No formal recommendation; officer only asked the panel to consider whether communication of year-end guidance changes was sufficient (para 40).
notes: Officer found no grounds to alter (para 39) but remitted to panel to weigh discretion; update says IPSA let overspend carry into 2021/22. Coded PARTIAL. Allocation of March goods purchase to 2020/21 was a categorical year-end rule, hence bright-line YES.

Value for money of custom canes judged case-by-case (paras 18-21). Officer consulted assessor and supplier after the refusal (paras 24, 26); one cane only, as estate use excluded (para 27); IPSA agreed 300 (para 31). Former-CEO advice discounted (para 21).

general_reading: Para 4.4 fixes which associated costs are claimable, so household items fall outside; household purchases are not directly linked to parliamentary functions, so para 10.19 discretion cannot apply (paras 21-22).
notes: MP relied on impression from IPSA induction meetings that reasonable start-up costs were claimable, backed by three colleagues (paras 10, 13); good faith accepted but claim refused. Items (bedding, towels, electricals) are absent from para 4.4 list: categorical.

guidance_change_note: CO suggests next Scheme edition explain budget pro-rating (Recommendation 1); IPSA CEO accepted and assured it would be addressed (para 41).
notes: Contingency panel refusal under para 10.10 criteria; CO finds circumstances not exceptional since tenancy ended before election called (paras 24, 39-40). Scheme silent on pro-rating when MP leaves rental mid-year (para 32). Bright-line NO: exceptional-circumstances test needs judgment.

Provisional report; para numbers jump 33 to 39. Overspend 2,940.01; itemised costs total about 2,350.80. 504 allowed, 1,846.88 refused with plea for leniency. Unclear whether office manager's advice evidence was before the panel. Exceptionality test needs judgment.

Provisional report (para 31 placeholder). Subject claims GBP90+GBP40; total overspend GBP2,940.01 (paras 5-6). Panel judged exceptionality, so not bright-line, though underlying rejections used 90-day/no-invoice/budget rules. Staff-advice contention not accepted by IPSA (para 22); Officer silent. Repayment-plan suggestion case-specific (para 30).

general_reading: MP, as employer, is responsible for ensuring staff are on the correct contract; IPSA terms apply only once a signed IPSA contract is returned to IPSA (paras 35, 42, 49).
guidance_change_note: Officer recommends IPSA personally contact all staff still on House of Commons contracts and log it; IPSA CEO accepted and undertook to address it (para 44; Recommendation 1).
notes: Footnote cites Eleventh edition; all editions reviewed (para 12). MP blamed IPSA for wrong contract (para 18); Officer rebutted using process facts gathered in review (paras 22-31, 38, 40). Commitment is a process step, not rule change. Contingency decision discretionary.

general_reading: Cleaning exclusion read as covering routine cleaning while an MP occupies the property, not a lease-mandated end-of-tenancy deep clean, which may count as a service charge (paras 24, 26-27).
guidance_change_note: Next Scheme edition should distinguish general cleaning from end-of-tenancy deep cleans and clarify what IPSA 'approval' of leases means (Review Recommendation 1; Appendix One).
notes: Edition 8 used; 11th/12th also cited. Para 24 general reading coexists with Appendix One precedent disclaimer. Service-charge basis was officer's own research. Panel applied categorical cleaning exclusion (bright-line YES). Lease-approval argument accepted; other-MP payments verified but not a listed reason.

general_reading: The para 4.5 cleaning exclusion covers routine cleaning during occupation, not an end-of-tenancy deep clean required by an IPSA-approved lease, which can be treated as a service charge (paras 24, 27).
guidance_change_note: Next Scheme edition should clarify what lease 'approval' means (para 4.21) and what service-charge claims are allowed (para 34, Recommendation); IPSA agreed to consider (Appendix One).
notes: Panel applied categorical cleaning exclusion (para 4.5), hence bright-line YES; officer reinterpreted it and relied on IPSA's lease approval. Non-precedent stated at para 34 and Appendix. Amount inconsistent (£710.40 para 15; £715.20 para 29). Rent item £85.48 dropped.

guidance_change_note: Closing review comment says confusion over when depreciation calculations are considered needs to be addressed (unnumbered comment after para 44).
notes: Panel accepted need but refused on value for money (para 22). Officer agreed, yet allowed 60 off, citing IPSA's prior email and six weeks' work use (paras 32-34, 39-41); figure used IT-team depreciation data gathered in review (paras 34, 48).

App. 2 reply to IPSA says ruling opens no floodgates; each case turns on its facts. Relied on confirmation, obtained at review, that invoice was emailed after account closure (paras 14, 27). Claim plainly late, but contingency test needs judgment.

general_reading: 'Exceptional circumstances' for contingency funding must arise in connection with the MP's parliamentary role, not personal circumstances; discretion outside the Scheme likewise needs a parliamentary-function link (paras 27, 52-53, 60).
notes: Two strands: circumstances personal not parliamentary (para 27); avoidable, based on CO's own later research into tenant's death date (para 28). MP's claim she followed IPSA/lawyer advice (para 43) not expressly addressed. Bright-line NO: exceptional/unavoidable tests need judgment.

expense_category: legal fees, vacant possession of property
general_reading: 'Exceptional' in the contingency test means circumstances arising from the MP's parliamentary role, not personal ones; para 4.14 moving legal costs cover in-office moves only (second-series paras 15, 19).
notes: Provisional report; paragraph numbering restarts at 3 on p.4, refs use second series. Claim first paid, then found ineligible post-payment; review targets contingency refusal, a judgment test, though underlying ineligibility of the cost type was categorical. Good faith accepted.

guidance_change_note: IPSA should consider amending the Scheme to cover short-term temporary accommodation chosen instead of hotels, especially for newly elected MPs (Review Recommendation; accepted, para 48).
notes: Panel's grounds were categorical (unsigned/unregistered tenancy, 90-day limit), so bright-line; Officer found exceptional circumstances (paras 45-46). Holiday-let nature clarified only on review (para 41). Claimed phone advice unverified (para 40); unanswered advice request credited (46b). IPSA accepted recommendation (para 48).

general_reading: Volunteer food costs are claimable only when tied to travel for volunteering and representing additional expense; lunches bought while working from home are ineligible (paras 21.12, 21.17, 22.2).
guidance_change_note: Officer finds volunteer-expense wording ambiguous and recommends IPSA clarify the Scheme and possibly the model volunteer form (paras 21.6, 22.4; Recommendation).
notes: MP said similar earlier claims were paid (para 17.2; App. 2 paras 37-38); Officer did not expressly address this, so REJECTED is implicit. Officer's web research was interpretive, not case facts. Scheme silent on location; refusal required interpretation (para 22.4).

guidance_change_note: IPSA should personally contact MPs affected by Scheme amendments and define 'unavoidable', e.g. evidence of landlord negotiation and alternatives considered (Review Recommendations 1-2).
notes: Disputed sum £311 (para 7); total rent owed later put at £1,594.44 (para 54). Written 2016 IPSA assurance decisive (paras 39, 48); 'unavoidable' given ordinary meaning (para 46). Panel met three times and wavered, so judgment was required.

general_reading: 'Unavoidable' in para 6.19 bears its ordinary meaning, not able to be prevented; a landlord's evidenced refusal to agree a two-month break clause can meet it (para 47).
guidance_change_note: No new recommendations; officer refers to those already made in a recent review on the same subject (para 58).
notes: Two-month cap is numeric but 'unless unavoidable' exception needs judgment, so not bright-line. Officer also weighed IPSA's 2015 reassurance, the mid-lease 2017 rule change and weak communication. Unclear whether landlord-refusal evidence was before the panel. 11th edition named as current.

general_reading: Payment-card costs are allocated to the budget year in which the transaction occurred, not the year the cost relates to, unless a year-end form is filed on time (paras 23, 25, 38).
guidance_change_note: Officer suggests IPSA consider clearer payment-card and year-end guidance and better MP access to payment information (paras 35, 39-40).
notes: Card payment 27 March 2017 fell in 2016-17; no year-end form by 13 April; 163.59 over budget: mechanically decidable. Edition question left undecided as immaterial (paras 19-20). Past-practice coding borderline: MP cited general IPSA email, prior-year card-limit practice (para 12).

general_reading: Claims are judged only within the Scheme's four corners; informal advice or approval-type statements by IPSA staff create no legitimate expectation, and the Scheme allows no prior approval (para 17).
guidance_change_note: Suggests IPSA restate that pre-claim advice is not approval, and give specific guidance on lease clauses requiring end-of-tenancy cleaning (paras 18-19).
notes: MP said winding-up meeting advice and an 'IPSA-approved' lease justified the claim, and that the exclusion meant day-to-day cleaning. Para 4.5a excludes cleaning categorically, though a first validator initially allowed it (para 6). Annex A letter read visually (image pages).

guidance_change_note: CO recommends IPSA staff be reminded to record all claim communications in CRM; backs extra record-keeping support for MP's office (Recommendations 1-2; accepted, para 52).
notes: Air fares (£330.41) upheld: invoices supplied after 30-day card deadline (paras 39, 47-48). Subsistence allowed at £300: IPSA mistakenly withheld hotel invoice and overlooked proxy's 7 March explanation (paras 44, 49-51). Original refusals applied deadline and £25 cap mechanically.

general_reading: IPSA may allocate a cost to the budget year in which the transaction occurred, not the year it relates to, unless year-end procedures were followed (paras 20, 32-34).
guidance_change_note: Officer suggests IPSA consider clearer payment-card and year-end guidance and better MP access to payment information (paras 30, 35, 36).
notes: Filename says Statement of Findings but it is a s.6A review; amended June 2018. Allocation by transaction date was rule-based (bright-line); discretion stage needed judgment. Edition question raised (paras 16-17) but held immaterial. Reliance was on supplier's assurance, not IPSA's.

general_reading: Bulk mailings to constituents that span multiple unrelated topics count as newsletters regardless of medium; the exclusion also reaches production and distribution costs such as mailing software (paras 27-28, 30).
notes: Claim auto-paid, passed post-payment review, then rejected after FOI-prompted scrutiny (paras 6-8). Rule 6.6c categorical and claim evidence itself said 'newsletter' (paras 28d, 30), so bright-line YES, though term undefined. Website evidence only corroborative. Advice reliance held irrelevant (para 26).

general_reading: Office costs cover only renting, equipping and running an office; paying third-party charges for constituents is a gift, not claimable even if no other funding exists (paras 36-39).
notes: Claims first paid via streamlined validation, then refused on post-payment check, repayment sought (paras 6-7). 25+ earlier similar claims allowed; Officer cites Scheme 2.3 that prior decisions do not bind (para 34). No explicit rule on such costs (para 35).

general_reading: Briefcases for paper documents cannot be distinguished from laptop bags; while IPSA allows laptop-bag claims it must equally allow briefcase claims (para 42).
guidance_change_note: Officer asks IPSA to review future laptop-bag and briefcase claims for uniform validator treatment (para 43); IPSA will consider implications (Appendix A).
notes: Claim paid unvalidated, then rejected post-payment with repayment sought. Officer, not MP, unearthed 19 paid laptop-bag claims (paras 32-34) and felt bound by that precedent (paras 41-43); OTHER = consistency of treatment. Reasonableness/'other citizens' tests needed judgment.

general_reading: Promoting local business is core to a constituency MP's role; where the Scheme gives MPs discretion IPSA should not override reasonable methods; merely advertising prizes does not bar a leaflet (paras 23, 25).
guidance_change_note: Officer invited IPSA to weigh this case in its ongoing Scheme review of 'parliamentary functions' and MP discretion (para 33); IPSA will consider implications (Annex C).
notes: Claim paid via streamlined validation, then rejected post-payment; debt cancelled. Outcome leaned on comparator claims by other MPs and identical 2015 claim. Annex C (image-only, read visually) shows IPSA accepting the determination. Radio-station logo criticised but not fatal (para 26).

Expense 10 March 2015; proxy entered 27 May, MP confirmed 15 June, after 30 May deadline (paras 28-32): date rule decides. Workload and RSA-token problems treated as mitigation only (paras 44-47). Annex E mentions IPSA IT-access work, not rule change.

general_reading: No Scheme rule governs fonts or colours, so IPSA cannot add such regulation to office-cost claims; leaflet content about councillors is not parliamentary so unclaimable (paras 29b, 30, 32).
notes: IPSA refused as political; officer held party affiliation, colour and font not determinative because every ward councillor appeared, but councillor content non-parliamentary, so half paid (IPSA argued a quarter). Pre-claim phone/email advice held outside review (para 29a). Annexes read visually.

MP said mailing was a meeting invitation mislabelled on invoice; CO found one side a newsletter, so not wholly parliamentary (paras 19-25). Claim paid first, refused after post-payment check, recovered by offsetting (paras 2-3). Categorical newsletter ban plus invoice label.

general_reading: Work supporting an MP's shadow-ministerial role is outside parliamentary functions and ordinarily Short Money-funded; work only partly parliamentary fails the wholly-exclusively-necessarily test (paras 27-28, 30).
notes: Amount derived from 525 disallowed plus 175 allowed (para 30). Officer used internet research, speech text and briefing supplied during review (paras 17-23). Parliamentary versus shadow-ministerial purpose needs judgment; Officer called the line blurred (para 19).

general_reading: Which Scheme edition governs depends on when the cost was incurred, not when it was paid; the review rests on the Scheme itself rather than IPSA guidance notes (paras 33-34).
notes: IPSA applied payment date per guidance (7th ed.); Officer applied date cost incurred, 2 Feb 2015 (6th ed.), and the Scheme alone (paras 25, 30-34). Dates were in the submission; categorical cutoff, so bright-line once governing date chosen.

general_reading: Mitigating circumstances (technical problems, election) fall outside the review, which is limited to whether IPSA decided in line with the Scheme and its procedures; year-end 60-day deadline applies (paras 24, 29-30).
notes: Amount summed by coder from five Annex A lines (text gives no total; table layout garbled). March 2015 costs submitted 15 June, after 30 May year-end deadline communicated three times (para 31). Bright-line: submission date versus fixed deadline.

Numeric nightly caps (£150 London/£120 elsewhere, para 4.31) applied to invoices, so bright-line. No record MP contacted IPSA at the time to seek discretion (paras 26, 29). Annex A line totals sum to £906.20 versus £888.20 in text.

Overspend is arithmetic against budget limits, re-verified by officer (paras 27, 29), hence bright-line YES. £78.70 of total uncontested (fn 3). IPSA admitted repeated errors and wrong advice; para 29 says debt to public purse stands regardless. Already repaid.

general_reading: Staff travel between a staff member's home office and Westminster is outside the 4th and 5th edition rules; where IPSA guidance differs from the Scheme, the Scheme governs (paras 32-36).
notes: Treated as s.6A review although claims already paid (paras 3-6). Bright-line mixed: caps/redaction/evidence categorical; home-office travel, 'unreasonable to return', no-show fees needed judgment. Officer criticised IPSA handling and absent written policy, invited reconsidering travel recovery (paras 43-44, 67-73).

general_reading: Para 9.2.a needs two stages: identify each journey (single only if essentially uninterrupted, judged by purpose), then test necessity for parliamentary functions; any non-parliamentary purpose generally disqualifies (paras 42-46).
guidance_change_note: Reports IPSA's Fifth edition (from 1 April 2013) newly allows diverted constituency-Westminster journeys, capped at direct standard open fare, after a 2012 consultation (paras 25-27).
notes: Scanned PDF; pdftotext gave 13 bytes, so all 13 pages read visually. Refusal covered 296.35; officer conceded second leg (272.45) after appeal, leaving 23.90, held properly refused. Agreed facts. Tribunal called both readings arguable; Fifth-edition argument rejected (paras 47-48).

guidance_change_note: CO said IPSA should consider the MP's print-media arguments at its next Scheme review and forwarded her letter for that purpose (para 8).
notes: MP did not dispute item was a newsletter; argued the print-newsletter ban is irrational and discriminatory (para 4, letter). CO applied guidance to para 10.4(e). CO found IPSA under-refused by £12.06 VAT but waived recovery as disproportionate (para 8).
